title: Creator study: @rahulmhinduja
creator: Rahul Hinduja (505K followers, tech / PC builds, Hinglish)
length: 12 reels studied (42–179 s each), posted 6–27 Oct 2026
one_liner: Number in the first second, something new every 1.2–2 s, yellow on black, and a comment keyword at the end.
why_it_matters: Rahul is the closest big creator to your tech/PC lane: Indian, Hinglish, PC builds by budget, filmed from one home set. Breaking down his 12 latest reels shows a repeatable system (hooks, layouts, pace, sound, covers, CTA) that you can copy in structure, and the data shows which of his formats bring loyal fans and which bring reach.

big_idea.statement: Rahul runs a fast, number-first Hinglish format: verdict in the first second, constant visual change, one brand colour, and a comment-to-DM funnel that delivers a living resource.
support: Every hook puts the topic and a number (price, score, date) on screen and in the voice within 1–2 s.
Something new appears on screen roughly every 1.2–2 s in every reel.
Yellow on black is his identity: labels, prices, banners, the face-cam ring.
Keyword-CTA reels get about 10× the comments-per-like of his one no-CTA reel.
PC builds bring the most loyal engagement; universal tech tricks bring the biggest reach.

chapters.title: Snapshot: who and the numbers
chapters.summary: Rahul Hinduja is a verified tech creator with about 505K followers and 1.3K posts; his bio reads 'Making tech easy :)'. He speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English captions and covers Indian PC-hardware buying advice plus everyday tech tricks. The study covers his 12 most recent reels (the listing caps at 12, so 12 of a planned 30), two of them pinned sponsored reels. Median plays are 202K (0.40× his followers). The mean is 1.21M only because one sponsored Flipkart reel hit 11.3M; without it the mean is 293K.

chapters.title: Pillars and the running story
chapters.summary: Four of ten organic reels are PC builds by budget (₹75K, ₹1L, ₹1.5L, ₹2L), all labelled 'October 2026', and they have his best like rates (4.8–5.3%). Two are PC buying help (CPU ratings, a shop checklist), two are everyday tech tricks or tool finds (widest reach), one is a how-it-works explainer and one is AI tips (his weakest). A running narrative ties the builds together: PC prices are rising every week because of AI data centres and the RAM crisis, so buy now. That gives each build a reason to exist this week and makes the series feel like live news.

chapters.title: Hooks: verdict first, no intro
chapters.summary: Every reel puts the topic and a number (price, score or date) on screen and in the voice within the first one or two seconds, with no greeting. The patterns: verdict first (name, price, score), 'do this right now' demos the viewer can try while watching, curiosity plus a tiny effort, hyper-local conditionals that name real markets, date-stamped mockery, contrarian 'don't buy X' spending advice, 'stop doing X' rants and sarcastic congratulations. Sponsored reels use tier framing or festive hype instead.

chapters.title: Layouts and pace
chapters.summary: He uses five layouts and most organic reels switch between them every few seconds. A: designed motion graphics on the top ~55% over a face cam (60 fps, smooth animation). B: full-frame talking head with yellow pop-up labels over the chest. C: screen or card full-frame with a circular yellow-ringed face cam and an app badge. D: a yellow banner on top with the face below. E: 1–3 s meme cutaways with the product or price pasted into the meme. Something new appears roughly every 1.2–2 s, and the sponsored Flipkart reel is fastest at 1.2 s.

chapters.title: Covers, text and colour
chapters.summary: Covers follow five types: a meme with a price tag (DiCaprio toast with '₹1,50,000 2K BUILD'), a data card (budget grid, receipt, rating card), a proof split ('SAME CODE' on phone and server), Hinglish provocation text, and a UI screenshot. The meme frames come from the reel's own payoff near the end, so the cover promises the ending. Rules that hold across all of them: a ₹ number or score whenever there is one, a face somewhere, and yellow as the accent. On screen, labels are heavy condensed caps in yellow, prices are big yellow ₹ figures, red means bad or price up and green means saved.

chapters.title: Sound
chapters.summary: All 12 reels measure −14 LUFS integrated with a loudness range of 2.2–4.8 LU, so the mix is heavily compressed and consistent. Fewer than 2.5% of 100 ms windows sit more than 25 dB under the median, meaning breaths and pauses are cut and there's no dead air. The quietest audio sits 9–21 dB below speech but never at true silence, which suggests a constant low bed of music, room tone or SFX (inferred, not confirmed by ear). The voice dominates, and none of the 12 uses trending audio.

blocks.text: For talking tech reels, voice-led with no trending song is fine; it lets the hook line carry. Save trending audio for gym montage reels where you aren't talking.

chapters.title: CTA: the comment-to-DM funnel
chapters.summary: Nearly every reel ends with 'Comment KEYWORD, I'll send it over', the keyword appearing in the caption and as a big yellow label in the last 2–4 seconds. The Layout-A reels show the funnel itself: a mock Instagram comment box with the keyword being typed, then a DM preview with the freebie attached. The freebies are living resources (live-price part lists, a full tier list, a component checklist), not a repeat of the video. His CPU ratings reel shows only six CPUs and flashes the full tier list, with 'Comment CPU for the rest'. The one organic reel with no CTA got about a tenth of the comments-per-like.

blocks.title: Withhold the remainder

blocks.text: Gym: 'Comment SPLIT' for your actual weekly split as a checklist. Tech: 'Comment BUILD' for your parts list with prices and dates. Show the mock comment and DM preview so they know what they'll get.

chapters.title: Outliers and what to copy
chapters.summary: The 11.3M Flipkart reel looks like paid amplification (0.3% like rate, 334 comments), so it isn't a benchmark. His best organic reel, the 1.2M Gmail one-word trick, works because its audience is everyone, the effort is tiny and testable on the spot, the URL bar is shown not told, and a strong freebie drove 2.7K comments. The 552K ₹1.5L gaming-and-streaming build is the best at scale for likes: a realistic budget, a contrarian '8 GB GPU is a waste' hook, proof on screen and a meme rhythm. The weakest (ChatGPT prompts debunk, the long Meld sponsor, a niche Photoshop alternative) leave viewers with less or sit off-pillar.

glossary.def: Plays divided by follower count; 1× means as many plays as followers.
Likes divided by plays; a rough measure of how much viewers liked it.
Comments divided by likes; jumps when there's a comment-keyword CTA.
A recurring content category a creator keeps returning to.
A named, repeatable series (e.g. 'PC Build – October 2026') refreshed on a schedule.
A freebie that stays useful and updates (live prices, a tier list), unlike a recap of the video.
Reach bought by a brand or platform; inflates plays but not engagement.
A small video of the creator's face over screen content.
A 1–3 s full-screen meme cut into the reel, often with the product pasted in.
A loudness unit; −14 LUFS is a common target for social and streaming audio.
Hindi and English mixed in one sentence.

try_it.title: A Rahul-style budget build

Fill a parts card slot by slot with prices and a budget bar.

try_it.title: Universal 'do this now' trick
steps: Find a tiny trick anyone can try in 10 seconds (an iPhone camera setting, a Windows shortcut).
Show it on screen with a circular face cam.
Keep it under 60 s; add a keyword CTA with a related freebie.
